meta.phase-name: Concrete Level Kinds, Fields, and Unreal Browser Plan

phase-plan.purpose: Turn the approved phase-58 model into concrete examples. This slice defines example level kinds, the default fields every level should have, when rooms apply, how towns/buildings/rooms nest, and what the first-pass Unreal level browser should show.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: example level taxonomy, baseline level fields, room applicability rules, town/building/room nesting, Unreal browser information architecture, and planning guidance for later schema/codegen work. Out of scope: implementation or final engine type definitions.
phase-plan.definition-of-done: Done when the planning docs contain recommended example level kinds, baseline level fields, room and building rules, and Unreal browser contents that the user can react to directly.

file.description: Current level-centered world model that this slice makes concrete.
Current Unreal workflow plan that this slice grounds into browser content and caveats.

task.description: Propose example level kinds aligned with the current model.
Propose a baseline field set for all levels.
Define when rooms are required, optional, or irrelevant, including how towns and buildings introduce rooms.
Propose the first-pass Unreal browser contents and user flow.

recommendation.proposal: Use four initial level kinds: `region`, `dungeon-floor`, `dungeon-region`, and `transition-level`.
recommendation.details: `region` contains town, wilderness, outskirts, and dungeon entrances. `dungeon-floor` uses rooms directly. `dungeon-region` does not use rooms directly and may contain towns, buildings, and sites inside the dungeon. `transition-level` handles travel gates, stairwells, boss thresholds, or short connector spaces.

recommendation.proposal: Every level should start with a shared baseline field set: `id`, `name`, `kind`, `theme`, `summary`, `tags`, `entryPoints`, `exitPoints`, `connections`, `entityRefs`, `contentRefs`, `dialogueRefs`, `questRefs`, `rules`, and `visualHints`.
recommendation.details: `entryPoints` and `exitPoints` define arrival and departure. `connections` links to other levels. `entityRefs`, `contentRefs`, `dialogueRefs`, and `questRefs` keep content attachment level-centric. `rules` carries flags like `usesRooms`, `usesBuildings`, or `isSafeZone`. `visualHints` carries biome, palette, tileset, and Unreal-facing hints.

recommendation.proposal: `dungeon-floor` requires rooms. `region` does not use rooms directly. `dungeon-region` does not use rooms directly. Rooms enter region-like play through building interiors rather than as a direct subdivision of the level.
recommendation.details: Towns may contain districts. Districts may contain buildings. Buildings may contain rooms. This preserves room reuse and precise placement while keeping region-like spaces honest.

recommendation.proposal: The browser should prioritize understanding the level before placement actions. Recommended order: `Overview`, `Content`, `Structure`, `Assets`, `Diagnostics`, then `Place`.
recommendation.details: `Overview` shows name, kind, theme, connected levels, and high-level composition. `Content` lists entities, dialogue, quests, items, encounters, and cutscenes. `Structure` shows towns, districts, buildings, sites, wilderness zones, outskirts zones, or rooms depending on level kind. `Assets` lists generated classes/data/assets. `Diagnostics` shows missing or unsupported content. `Place` supports drag-drop first, with managed placement later. This workflow targets `plugins/DB_Unreal_DLC_Plugin`.

recommendation.proposal: Generate as much as possible from the schema first. For Escape the Dungeon, details that are not yet worth making generically authorable may remain hardcoded temporarily.
recommendation.details: This keeps the game moving while the schema and level model mature. The goal is not a full editor for every detail before gameplay continues.

questions.question: Initial recommended level kinds: `region`, `dungeon-floor`, `dungeon-region`, and `transition-level`.
Every level needs a baseline field set so loading, transitions, content lookup, and Unreal browsing can work consistently.
`region` and `dungeon-region` do not use rooms directly. `dungeon-floor` uses rooms directly. Towns may contain districts, districts may contain buildings, and buildings may contain rooms.
The Unreal level browser should prioritize understanding generated level content first, then browsing assets/content groups, then drag-drop or later managed placement actions.

decision.summary: The approved level-centered model still needs concrete examples and field guidance before it is useful for schema and plugin work.
decision.impact: Phase 58 remains planning-active until the model is concrete enough to guide later implementation.

decision.summary: The initial recommended level kinds are `region`, `dungeon-floor`, `dungeon-region`, and `transition-level`.
decision.impact: Gives the schema and game runtime a small but expressive starting taxonomy that matches the current design direction.

decision.summary: Region-like levels do not expose rooms directly. Room structure enters through building interiors, especially towns and similar contained locations.
decision.impact: Allows room reuse and detailed placement without forcing every region-like level into direct room topology.

decision.summary: Towns may contain districts as an optional structural layer before buildings.
decision.impact: Lets town authoring scale up without forcing a flat town-to-building structure.

decision.summary: The Unreal browser should lead with understanding the selected level and its generated content before exposing placement actions.
decision.impact: Makes the first plugin workflow easier to understand and reduces confusion compared with leading directly with placement tooling.

decision.summary: The Unreal implementation target for this planning work is the `plugins/DB_Unreal_DLC_Plugin` submodule.
decision.impact: Keeps later execution grounded in the actual plugin repo instead of an abstract destination.

decision.summary: Escape the Dungeon can hardcode non-schema details temporarily after generating as much as possible from the schema.
decision.impact: Keeps the game moving while the schema-driven parts grow in coverage.

suggestion.gap: REQUIREMENTS.xml does not yet capture example level kinds, common level fields, district/building/room nesting, the Unreal plugin target repo, or the pragmatic Escape the Dungeon execution rule.
suggestion.proposal: Add requirements for the initial supported level kinds, the default field set shared by all levels, how towns may contain districts and buildings with rooms, that the Unreal workflow targets `plugins/DB_Unreal_DLC_Plugin`, and that Escape the Dungeon may hardcode non-schema details after schema generation where necessary.
